item.title: The Inverse of Right-continuous or Left-continuous Function
item.description: The inverses of a left-continuous function and a right-continuous function differ in a very subtle way. The inverse of a left-continuous function can be defined in two ways: \[G^{-1}(w) = \sup\{ y: G(y) < w\} \quad \text{or} \quad G^{-1}(w) = \inf\{y: G(y) \geq w\}\] The inverse of a right-continuous function can be defined in two ways: \[F^{-1}(w) = \sup\{ y: F(y) \leq w\} \quad \text{or} \quad F^{-1}(w) = \inf\{y: F(y) > w\}\]
